title: Britain's Tennis Team Fights Hard but Falls to Czech Republic in Billie Jean King Cup
summary:
Imagine playing tennis for three whole hours. Your back hurts. You haven't played a real match in six months. That's what Sonay Kartal did for Great Britain in the Billie Jean King Cup.

Kartal faced Marie Bouzkova from the Czech Republic. The Czech team was favored — all five of their players are ranked higher than any British player. Kartal fought hard, even saving three match points. But she lost a close one: 7-6, 4-6, 6-4.

Next up was Katie Boulter, Britain's top player. She faced Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova. Boulter lost 6-2, 7-6. That meant Britain was out of the tournament.

"It was always going to be a tough challenge against the Czechs," said captain Anne Keothavong. "I can't fault their efforts."

Kartal said the match gave her confidence for the rest of the season. "These events are my favourite, but they also sting the most," she said.

The Czech Republic moves on to the semi-finals. Britain's wait for a first title continues.
why_it_matters: It shows that in team sports you can lose even when you give everything — and that finding confidence in a tough match, like Kartal did, is part of being an athlete.

background_read: The Billie Jean King Cup is the biggest yearly team competition in women's tennis, named after Billie Jean King (a famous American tennis champion who also pushed hard for women's sport to get fair treatment).

Great Britain (the country that includes England, Scotland and Wales) has never won the title, while the Czech Republic (a country in central Europe) has long been one of the strongest teams in the competition.
Wimbledon (the most famous tennis competition in the world, played in London every summer) is where Linda Noskova is known as a champion.
